blurb: Everyday science from the periodic table to the kitchen counter

questions.q: Which noble gas shares its name with Superman's home planet?
questions.fact: Krypton's name comes from the Greek word kryptos, meaning hidden. It was discovered in 1898.
questions.src: chemicool.com/elements/krypton.html (Ramsay and Travers, London, 1898; Greek kryptos = hidden)

questions.q: In Iron Man 2 (2010), which element in Tony Stark's arc reactor is slowly poisoning him?
questions.fact: Palladium is a real precious metal, and one of its biggest uses is in car catalytic converters.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron_Man_2 (palladium core slowly poisoning him); livescience.com 36991-palladium (main use since 1989 is car catalytic converters)

questions.q: Helium was first detected in 1868, not on Earth, but where?
questions.fact: It's named after Helios, the Greek sun god. William Ramsay first isolated it on Earth in 1895.
questions.src: smithsonianmag.com how-scientists-discovered-helium-first-alien-element-1868 (Janssen, Aug 18 1868 eclipse, solar spectrum; Palmieri saw its line in Vesuvius lava 1882; Ramsay isolated it 1895)

questions.q: Which solid metal will melt in your hand, since it turns liquid at about 86 F (30 C)?
questions.fact: Mendeleev predicted gallium before French chemist Lecoq de Boisbaudran discovered it in 1875.
questions.src: chemicool.com/elements/gallium.html (mp 29.76 C / 85.6 F; Mendeleev eka-aluminum; Lecoq de Boisbaudran 1875)

questions.q: What gas makes baking soda and vinegar fizz when you mix them?
questions.fact: It's the same gas that puts the bubbles in soda and helps yeast bread rise.
questions.src: Textbook chemistry (acid-base reaction releases CO2)

questions.q: Cornstarch-and-water goo, named after a Dr. Seuss book, is known as what?
questions.fact: It's a non-Newtonian fluid: it pours like a liquid but stiffens when you punch or squeeze it.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oobleck (named after Bartholomew and the Oobleck; non-Newtonian starch-in-water suspension)

questions.q: Which acid gives vinegar its sour taste?
questions.fact: Lemons get their sourness from citric acid, and yogurt gets its tangy taste from lactic acid.
questions.src: healthline.com/nutrition/sour-foods (acetic acid is the main reason vinegar tastes sour; citric acid in citrus; lactic acid gives yogurt its sour taste). Replaced Maillard question, which duplicated A6's Maillard question

questions.q: Pop Rocks hit stores in 1975, but its 1956 inventor was trying to create what?
questions.fact: The same General Foods chemist, William Mitchell, also invented Tang and Cool Whip.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_A._Mitchell (1956 instantly self-carbonating soda attempt; Pop Rocks sold from 1975; Tang 1957; Cool Whip 1967; General Foods 1941-76)

questions.q: How many colors are in the traditional list of rainbow colors?
questions.fact: Isaac Newton started with five, then added orange and indigo to match the seven notes of a musical scale.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ROYGBIV ('Originally he used only five colors, but later he added orange and indigo' to match the major scale)

questions.q: In 2015, 'The Dress' photo split the internet. What colors was the real dress?
questions.fact: Retailer Roman Originals confirmed it was royal blue with black lace. The photo's lighting fooled many eyes.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_dress (royal blue Lace Bodycon Dress, black lace; Roman Originals tweet confirmed blue and black)

questions.q: The viral 2018 'Yanny or Laurel' clip was originally a recording of which word?
questions.fact: It came from a 2007 Vocabulary.com recording. Listeners tuned to higher frequencies heard Yanny.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yanny_or_Laurel (word laurel, recorded 2007 for Vocabulary.com by Jay Aubrey Jones; Yanny in higher frequencies)

questions.q: Which 1973 Pink Floyd album cover shows white light splitting into colors through a prism?
options: The Dark Side of the Moon
questions.fact: A prism splits white light because each color bends by a slightly different amount as it passes through.
questions.src: pentagram.com/work/the-dark-side-of-the-moon (prism design, Hipgnosis/George Hardie); dispersion is textbook optics

blurb: Speed demons, giants and the wild habits of Earth's creatures

questions.q: What is the fastest land animal on Earth?
questions.fact: Unlike lions and tigers, cheetahs can't roar. They purr, chirp and growl instead.
questions.src: clevelandzoosociety.org 2023/12/01 ask-the-expert-what-sounds-do-cheetahs-make (purrs, chirps, trills, growls, hisses; cannot roar); cheetah fastest land animal textbook

questions.q: In Disney's Zootopia (2016), the DMV is famously staffed by which slow-moving animals?
questions.fact: Real sloths move so little that algae grow in their fur, giving them a greenish tint.
questions.src: Zootopia DMV scene with Flash the sloth (textbook film fact); BMC Evol Biol 2010 10:86 (green algae, Trichophilus, growing in sloth hair)

questions.q: The roadrunner, speedy star of classic Looney Tunes cartoons, belongs to which bird family?
questions.fact: The roadrunner is New Mexico's state bird, and it's quick enough to catch and eat rattlesnakes.
questions.src: nps.gov/whsa/learn/nature/roadrunner.htm (cuckoo family; eats rattlesnakes; NM state bird)

questions.q: What is the fastest land animal native to North America?
questions.fact: Pronghorn are the last surviving members of their animal family, and they live only in North America.
questions.src: nps.gov/wica/learn/nature/pronghorn.htm ('fastest North American land mammal'; only surviving member of Antilocapridae; North America and nowhere else)

questions.q: What is the tallest animal on Earth?
questions.fact: A giraffe's long neck has just seven bones, the same number as a human neck.
questions.src: Textbook zoology (giraffe; seven cervical vertebrae)

questions.q: The capybara, a South American internet favorite, is the world's largest what?
questions.fact: Capybaras are excellent swimmers and have slightly webbed feet.
questions.src: buffalozoo.org/animal/capybara (largest rodents; excellent swimmers; partially webbed feet)

questions.q: The bee hummingbird, the world's smallest bird, lives in the wild only in which country?
questions.fact: Adults are only about 2 inches long, from beak to tail.
questions.src: hummingbirdcentral.com/bee-hummingbird.htm (endemic to Cuba; 2.24 in / 5.7 cm including bill)

questions.q: What is the largest living reptile on Earth?
questions.fact: Komodo dragons are the largest living lizards, but a big saltwater crocodile outweighs one many times over.
questions.src: Textbook zoology (Crocodylus porosus largest living reptile; Komodo largest lizard)

questions.q: Wild giant pandas eat almost nothing but what?
questions.fact: Pandas are true bears with a meat-eater's digestive system, so they must spend much of the day eating.
questions.src: Textbook zoology (Ailuropoda, family Ursidae; carnivore-type gut, bamboo diet)

questions.q: A famous 2016 Planet Earth II scene showed baby iguanas racing to escape swarms of what?
questions.fact: The chase was filmed on Fernandina Island in the Galapagos, and David Attenborough narrated it.
questions.src: discoverwildlife.com racer-snakes-versus-iguana-wins-bafta (filmed on Fernandina, Galapagos, for the opening Islands episode); galapagosconservation.org.uk (marine iguana hatchling vs Galapagos racer snakes)

questions.q: In 1960, Jane Goodall saw wild chimps do something thought to be uniquely human. What was it?
questions.fact: A chimp she named David Greybeard stripped the leaves off a stem and used it to fish termites from a mound.
questions.src: history.com this-day-in-history jane-goodall-observes-a-chimpanzee-making-and-using-tools (Nov 4 1960, Gombe; David Greybeard stripped leaves from a stem to fish termites; ability believed exclusive to humans)

questions.q: Born Free (1966) told the true story of Elsa, a lioness raised and released in which country?
questions.fact: It's based on Joy Adamson's 1960 bestseller about raising Elsa with her husband, George.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elsa_the_lioness (book 1960, film 1966); kenyans.co.ke 43047 (raised by the Adamsons, released into Meru National Park, Kenya)

blurb: Bats, owls, spiders and bugs: the night shift of the natural world

questions.q: What is the only mammal capable of true flight?
questions.fact: Roughly one in every five mammal species on Earth is a bat.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bat ('only mammals capable of true and sustained flight'; about 20% of classified mammal species)

questions.q: Which owl is famous for its pale, heart-shaped face?
questions.fact: That dish-like face funnels sound to its ears, letting it catch prey in total darkness by hearing alone.
questions.src: collections.museumsvictoria.com.au/species/6167 (heart-shaped facial disc; sound channelled to the ears; pinpoints prey in complete darkness); Konishi, J Exp Biol 54:535 (locates prey in total darkness by hearing alone). Replaced Hedwig/snowy owl question, which overlapped A7's Hedwig question

questions.q: About how far can an owl turn its head in either direction?
questions.fact: Owls can't move their eyes in their sockets, so they swivel their whole heads instead.
questions.src: sciencedaily.com/releases/2013/01/130131144102.htm (Johns Hopkins: up to 270 degrees in either direction); nationalgeographic.com how-owls-twist-heads-almost-360-degrees (fixed eye sockets, eyeballs can't rotate)

questions.q: Which city's Congress Avenue Bridge is home to a huge summer colony of Mexican free-tailed bats?
questions.fact: The bats moved in after the bridge was rebuilt, when narrow gaps under its new deck made perfect roosts.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ann_W._Richards_Congress_Avenue_Bridge (Mexican free-tailed bats roost in gaps under the road deck); 99percentinvisible.org episode 432 transcript (bats arrived shortly after the bridge was rebuilt)

questions.q: How many legs does a spider have?
questions.fact: Spiders aren't insects. They're arachnids, a group that also includes scorpions, ticks and mites.
questions.src: Textbook biology

questions.q: In the 1952 children's book Charlotte's Web, Charlotte is what kind of spider?
questions.fact: Her full name, Charlotte A. Cavatica, comes from the barn spider's scientific name, Araneus cavaticus.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barn_spider (basis for Charlotte; full name Charlotte A. Cavatica from Araneus cavaticus)

questions.q: Under an ultraviolet blacklight, what color do scorpions glow?
questions.fact: One theory is that the glow helps scorpions sense dim moonlight and find shady places to hide.
questions.src: nationalgeographic.com why-do-scorpions-glow-in-the-dark (blue-green under UV; Douglas Gaffin's hypothesis: light sensing, shade indicates hiding place)

questions.q: Many tarantulas defend themselves by flicking what at attackers?
questions.fact: They kick itchy hairs off their abdomen with their legs. Some female tarantulas live 20 years or more.
questions.src: blueplanetaquarium.com 6-fun-facts-about-tarantulas (flick urticating bristles at threats; females known to live up to 30 years); New World tarantulas kick hairs off abdomen, textbook

questions.q: In Pixar's A Bug's Life (1998), the inventive hero Flik is what kind of insect?
questions.fact: In a real ant colony, all of the worker ants are female.
questions.src: A Bug's Life (Pixar, 1998), Flik is an ant; worker ants are female, textbook

questions.q: In 2020, Washington State crews found and removed the first US nest of which giant insect?
questions.fact: Entomologists tracked it to a tree in Blaine by tying tiny radio tags to captured hornets with dental floss.
questions.src: ksat.com 2020/10/23 washington-state-discovers-first-murder-hornet-nest-in-us (first US nest; tree cavity in Blaine; found Oct 22 2020; radio trackers tied on with dental floss)

questions.q: Fireflies aren't actually flies. What kind of insect are they?
questions.fact: Many firefly species flash in their own pattern, which helps them find others of their own kind.
questions.src: Textbook entomology (Lampyridae are beetles)

questions.q: Periodical cicadas emerge in the eastern US every 13 years, or every how many years?
questions.fact: In 2024, 17-year Brood XIII and 13-year Brood XIX emerged in the same year for the first time since 1803.
questions.src: smithsonianmag.com cicadas-are-coming-rare-dual-emergence 180983635 (XIII and XIX together for first time since 1803); KING5 fact-check (13-year XIX, 17-year XIII; other 13/17 pairs co-emerge every 5-6 years, so original 'a 13-year and a 17-year brood' wording was misleading)

blurb: Missions, planets and stars, from Apollo to SpaceX

questions.q: Which famous space telescope was carried into orbit by the Space Shuttle in 1990?
questions.fact: Its blurry vision was fixed in 1993, when spacewalking astronauts installed corrective optics.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/STS-31 (launched Apr 24 1990, Hubble deployed Apr 25); esahubble.org servicing_mission_1 (Dec 1993 STS-61 installed COSTAR and WFPC2 corrective optics; mirror itself not repaired)

questions.q: Which 1970 Apollo mission had to skip its Moon landing after an oxygen tank exploded?
questions.fact: The crew made it home safely, and Tom Hanks played commander Jim Lovell in the 1995 film.
questions.src: NASA history (Apollo 13, April 1970); Apollo 13 film (1995)

questions.q: In 2020, which company's Crew Dragon capsule flew NASA astronauts to the space station?
questions.fact: It was the first crewed orbital launch from US soil since the Space Shuttle retired in 2011.
questions.src: spacepolicyonline.com two-american-astronauts-lift-off-from-american-soil-for-first-time-in-nine-years (Demo-2, May 30 2020; first from US soil since final shuttle mission 2011)

questions.q: The two Voyager probes, launched in 1977, each carry a golden record holding what?
questions.fact: Carl Sagan led the team that chose its contents, which include Chuck Berry's Johnny B. Goode.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voyager_Golden_Record (committee chaired by Carl Sagan; natural sounds and music; Johnny B. Goode included)

questions.q: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.fact: Its red color comes from iron oxide, basically rust, in its dusty soil.
questions.src: Textbook astronomy

questions.q: In what year was Pluto reclassified as a dwarf planet?
questions.fact: Pluto had been counted as the ninth planet ever since Clyde Tombaugh discovered it in 1930.
questions.src: earthsky.org pluto-dwarf-planet-august-24-2006 (IAU, Aug 24 2006); Tombaugh discovery 1930, textbook

questions.q: Which planet has the hottest surface in our solar system?
questions.fact: Venus beats Mercury because its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat like a greenhouse.
questions.src: Textbook astronomy (Venus surface about 465 C)

questions.q: Which planet spins tipped over on its side, rolling around the Sun like a ball?
questions.fact: Uranus was the first planet discovered with a telescope, found by William Herschel in 1781.
questions.src: science.gsfc.nasa.gov solar-system-tour Uranus ('first planet discovered by telescope', Herschel 1781; tilt 98 degrees)

questions.q: The Big Dipper is part of which constellation?
questions.fact: The two stars at the end of its bowl point the way to Polaris, the North Star.
questions.src: Textbook astronomy (Big Dipper asterism in Ursa Major; pointer stars Dubhe and Merak)

questions.q: Halley's Comet, last seen from Earth in 1986, returns about every how many years?
questions.fact: Edmond Halley predicted it would come back in 1758. It did, proving some comets orbit the Sun.
questions.src: science.nasa.gov/solar-system/comets/1p-halley (average period 76 years; last seen 1986; Halley correctly predicted 1758 return)

questions.q: A light-year is a unit used to measure what?
questions.fact: One light-year, the distance light travels in a year, is about 5.9 trillion miles.
questions.src: Textbook astronomy (about 5.88 trillion miles)

questions.q: In 2019, astronomers released the first-ever image of what?
questions.fact: The Event Horizon Telescope captured the black hole in galaxy M87, about 55 million light-years away.
questions.src: earthsky.org 1st-photo-black-hole-event-horizon-release-apr-2019 (Apr 10 2019; M87; 55 million light-years)

blurb: Sea creatures, the deepest trench and the pull of the tides

questions.q: What is the largest animal known to have ever lived?
questions.fact: Despite their size, blue whales live mostly on krill, tiny shrimp-like animals.
questions.src: Textbook marine biology

questions.q: Clownfish like the star of Finding Nemo (2003) make their homes in what?
questions.fact: A special coating on their skin protects clownfish from the anemone's stinging tentacles.
questions.src: Textbook marine biology (clownfish-anemone symbiosis)

questions.q: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.fact: Octopus blood is blue, thanks to a copper-based protein called hemocyanin.
questions.src: sciencefocus.com why-does-an-octopus-have-more-than-one-heart (three hearts; copper-rich haemocyanin makes blood blue)

questions.q: SpongeBob SquarePants is a sea sponge. What are real sea sponges?
questions.fact: Sponges have no brain, heart or muscles, and they're among the oldest animal groups on Earth.
questions.src: Textbook biology (phylum Porifera)

questions.q: What is the name of the deepest known ocean trench on Earth?
questions.fact: Its deepest point, the Challenger Deep, lies nearly 7 miles below the surface.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mariana_Trench (Challenger Deep 10,935 m, about 6.79 mi)

questions.q: The deep-sea anglerfish attracts prey in total darkness using what?
questions.fact: In many species, the glow comes from light-making bacteria living inside the lure.
questions.src: naturestories.org from-the-depths (symbiotic luminescent bacteria live in the esca)

questions.q: In 2012, which film director piloted a solo dive to the deepest point in the ocean?
questions.fact: The only earlier crewed dive there was in 1960, when Don Walsh and Jacques Piccard rode down in the Trieste.
questions.src: guinnessworldrecords.com first-dive-to-the-challenger-deep-by-a-crewed-vessel-solo (Cameron, Mar 2012); nationalgeographic.com 120324 (Walsh and Piccard, Trieste 1960, only humans before). Uncrewed probes had visited earlier, so fact now says 'crewed'

questions.q: Ocean explorer Jacques Cousteau co-invented which diving device, first tested in 1943?
questions.fact: Built with engineer Emile Gagnan, it made modern scuba diving possible.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Cousteau (co-invented Aqua-Lung with Emile Gagnan; first prototype tried 1943)

questions.q: What mainly causes the ocean's tides?
questions.fact: The Sun pulls too. When the Sun and Moon line up, we get extra-high spring tides.
questions.src: Textbook oceanography

questions.q: On most coastlines, how many high tides come in each day?
questions.fact: Tides arrive about 50 minutes later each day, because the Moon rises later each day too.
questions.src: oceanservice.noaa.gov tutorial_tides supp_tide05 (two high and two low tides every 24 h 50 min; Earth takes an extra 50 minutes to catch up to the Moon)

questions.q: In 2021, National Geographic officially recognized which as the world's fifth ocean?
questions.fact: It surrounds Antarctica and is defined by a current that flows all the way around the globe.
questions.src: abc7news.com world-oceans-day-2021-fifth-ocean (NatGeo, June 8 2021); nationalgeographic.com theres-a-new-ocean-now ('the Southern Ocean is defined by a current', the Antarctic Circumpolar Current)

questions.q: Which explorer gave the Pacific Ocean its name, meaning 'peaceful'?
questions.fact: Magellan named it in 1520 after calm sailing. Balboa had sighted it in 1513 and called it the South Sea.
questions.src: neatlinemaps.com 2018-2-12 ferdinand-magellan-and-the-renaming-of-the-south-sea (Magellan named it for calm waters after the strait, 1520; Balboa's Mar del Sur); Balboa 1513 textbook

blurb: Bones, senses and organs: a tour of the amazing machine you live in

questions.q: What is the longest bone in the human body?
questions.fact: The femur, or thigh bone, is also one of the strongest bones in the body.
questions.src: Textbook anatomy

questions.q: How many bones are in the typical adult human body?
questions.fact: Babies start out with closer to 300 bones, and many of them fuse together as they grow.
questions.src: popsci.com bones-human-skeleton (newborns can have more than 300 bones; adults typically 206)

questions.q: When you bang your 'funny bone,' what are you actually hitting?
questions.fact: It's the ulnar nerve, which passes close to the skin at your elbow.
questions.src: Textbook anatomy (ulnar nerve at the medial epicondyle)

questions.q: Which bone in the throat is the only bone not connected to any other bone?
questions.fact: The U-shaped hyoid is held in place by muscles and ligaments, and it helps support the tongue.
questions.src: my.clevelandclinic.org/health/body/hyoid-bone (only bone that doesn't connect to another bone; U-shaped; supports tongue)

questions.q: What is the colored part of the eye called?
questions.fact: The iris works like a camera shutter, widening or shrinking the pupil to control light.
questions.src: Textbook anatomy

questions.q: The 'red-eye' in old flash photos is light bouncing off what?
questions.fact: Many cameras fight it with a quick pre-flash that makes your pupils shrink first.
questions.src: Textbook optics (flash reflects off the blood-rich fundus/choroid at the back of the eye)

questions.q: The body's smallest bone is found in which part of the body?
questions.fact: Called the stapes, or stirrup, it's only about 3 millimeters long, smaller than a grain of rice.
questions.src: guinnessworldrecords.com smallest-bone (stapes, middle ear, 2.6-3.4 mm). Original 'size of a grain of rice' overstated it

questions.q: Along with sweet, sour, salty and bitter, what is considered the fifth basic taste?
questions.fact: Japanese chemist Kikunae Ikeda named it in 1908 after studying the savory taste of seaweed broth.
questions.src: ajinomoto.com.my/about-umami (Ikeda identified glutamate in kombu dashi and named umami in 1908)

questions.q: What is the largest organ of the human body?
questions.fact: The liver is the largest organ inside the body.
questions.src: Textbook anatomy

questions.q: How many chambers does the human heart have?
questions.fact: A typical heart beats around 100,000 times a day.
questions.src: livescience.com 44460-heart-facts ('The human heart beats about 100,000 times a day'); four chambers textbook

questions.q: Smartwatches like the Apple Watch track your pulse by shining what onto your wrist?
questions.fact: Blood absorbs green light, so the watch counts beats as the blood flow in your wrist rises and falls.
questions.src: support.apple.com HT204666 (green LEDs, photoplethysmography; blood reflects red and absorbs green light)

questions.q: Your left lung is a bit smaller than your right one. What does it make room for?
questions.fact: The right lung has three lobes, while the left lung has only two.
questions.src: Textbook anatomy (cardiac notch)

blurb: Dogs, cats and the small critters we share our homes with

questions.q: What breed of dog is Scooby-Doo?
questions.fact: Despite its name, the Great Dane was developed in Germany, not Denmark.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Dane (origin Germany); Scooby-Doo is a Great Dane, textbook

questions.q: TV's Lassie, which debuted in 1954, was what breed of dog?
questions.fact: Pal, who first played Lassie in a 1943 film, was male, and so were his descendants who played her on TV.
questions.src: cbsnews.com lassies-revival (role 'has always been played by a male dog'; Pal starred in the 1943 film; descendants of Pal); en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pal_(dog) (male Rough Collie)

questions.q: The 'Doge' meme that took off in 2013 starred which dog breed?
questions.fact: The Shiba Inu is the smallest of the six original dog breeds native to Japan.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shiba_Inu ('smallest of the six original dog breeds native to Japan'; Doge meme 2013, Kabosu)

questions.q: Which dog breed is famous for its blue-black tongue?
questions.fact: Chow Chow puppies are born with pink tongues, which turn blue-black as they grow.
questions.src: akc.org why-do-chow-chows-have-blue-tongues (puppies have pink tongues; only other breed with the requirement is the Shar-Pei, not an option)

questions.q: Which comic-strip cat, created in 1978, is famous for loving lasagna?
questions.fact: Creator Jim Davis named him after his grandfather, James Garfield Davis.
questions.src: ballstatedaily.com 2018/08 news-jim-davis-centennial (named after his grandfather, James Garfield Davis, per the Garfield website); strip began June 1978

questions.q: Which cat breed is best known for being hairless?
questions.fact: Despite its Egyptian-sounding name, the modern breed began in Toronto, Canada, in 1966.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sphynx_cat ('started in 1966 in Toronto, Ontario, Canada')

questions.q: The Manx, a cat breed known for having no tail, comes from which island?
questions.fact: Some Manx cats have a short stub of a tail, while those called rumpies have none at all.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manx_cat (Isle of Man; rumpies have no tail, stumpies a short stub)

questions.q: Which basic taste can cats not detect?
questions.fact: Cats lack a working gene for sweet taste receptors, so sugar simply doesn't register.
questions.src: scientificamerican.com strange-but-true-cats-cannot-taste-sweets (Tas1r2 gene defect); catster.com how-do-cats-taste (cats taste all basic flavors except sweet, so Salty/Sour/Bitter are wrong)

questions.q: Where do hamsters stash extra food so they can carry it home?
questions.fact: Syrian, or golden, hamsters are loners and are usually happiest living alone.
questions.src: rvc.ac.uk Caring-for-your-hamster 2022 (golden/Syrian hamsters housed singly; cheek pouches); textbook

questions.q: Despite their name, guinea pigs originally come from where?
questions.fact: They were domesticated in the Andes mountains thousands of years ago.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guinea_pig (domesticated in the Andean region of South America as early as 5000 BC)

questions.q: Sea-Monkeys, sold through comic book ads in the 1960s, are actually what?
questions.fact: The comic ads showed smiling humanlike creatures that looked nothing like the real tiny shrimp.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea-Monkeys (brand of Artemia brine shrimp; von Braunhut 1957; 1960s comic ads drew humanoid creatures)

questions.q: Which smiling salamander, a popular pet, was added to Minecraft in 2021?
questions.fact: Wild axolotls come from lakes near Mexico City, and they can regrow lost limbs.
questions.src: pcgamer.com minecraft-cave-cliffs-update (Part 1 launched June 8 2021, added axolotls); aquariumofpacific.org axolotl (Xochimilco, Chalco and Chapultepec lakes near Mexico City; regenerate limbs). 'Gecko' (a lizard) replaced with Hellbender so all options are salamanders

blurb: Dinosaurs, fossil hunters and the prehistoric beasts that weren't dinos

questions.q: The word 'dinosaur' comes from Greek words meaning what?
questions.fact: British scientist Richard Owen coined the word in 1842.
questions.src: nhm.ac.uk how-dinosaurs-got-their-name (Owen, 1842 report; usually rendered 'terrible lizard')

questions.q: Jurassic Park's (1993) Velociraptors were really modeled on which larger dinosaur?
questions.fact: Real Velociraptors stood only about 1.6 feet tall at the hip, and fossils show they had feathers.
questions.src: livescience.com 23922-velociraptor-facts (about 1.6 ft / 0.5 m at the hip; 2007 quill knobs; movie raptors modeled after Deinonychus). Original 'about 2 feet tall' was loose

questions.q: How many fingers did each Tyrannosaurus rex hand have?
questions.fact: T. rex lived closer in time to us than to Stegosaurus.
questions.src: daily.jstor.org five-things-you-probably-have-wrong-about-the-t-rex (T. rex lived closer to the modern day than to Stegosaurus); two-fingered hands textbook

questions.q: A Stegosaurus's spiked tail is nicknamed what, thanks to a 1982 Far Side cartoon?
questions.fact: Paleontologist Ken Carpenter adopted Gary Larson's joke word in 1993, and it caught on with scientists.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thagomizer (1982 Far Side; first adopted by Kenneth Carpenter at the 1993 SVP meeting)

questions.q: A scientist who studies fossils of ancient life is called a what?
questions.fact: Archaeologists dig up human history. Dinosaurs vanished some 66 million years before people arrived.
questions.src: Textbook science

questions.q: Sue, one of the most complete T. rex skeletons ever found, is on display in which city?
questions.fact: Sue was found in South Dakota in 1990 and named after the fossil hunter who spotted it, Sue Hendrickson.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sue_(dinosaur) (found Aug 12 1990, South Dakota, by Sue Hendrickson; named after her; Field Museum, Chicago)

questions.q: Which pioneering fossil hunter made famous finds on the cliffs of Lyme Regis, England, in the early 1800s?
questions.fact: Her hunting ground is now part of England's Jurassic Coast, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
questions.src: nationalgeographic.com mary-anning-forgotten-fossil-hunter-british-jurassic-coast (Lyme Regis; ichthyosaur 1811; Jurassic Coast UNESCO site)

questions.q: In 2016, scientists revealed a feathered dinosaur tail preserved inside what?
questions.fact: The tail was about 99 million years old and came from amber mined in Myanmar.
questions.src: nationalgeographic.com feathered-dinosaur-tail-amber-theropod-myanmar-burma-cretaceous (99 million years; Hukawng Valley amber, Myanmar)

questions.q: In the 2002 film Ice Age, Manny is what kind of prehistoric animal?
questions.fact: A few woolly mammoths survived on Wrangel Island until about 4,000 years ago, after the Great Pyramid was built.
questions.src: Ice Age (2002), Manny is a mammoth; ipm.org amomentofscience 2020-02-06 the-last-woolly-mammoths (Wrangel Island until about 4,000 years ago, while Egyptians were building pyramids); Great Pyramid about 2560 BC

questions.q: The La Brea Tar Pits, famous for saber-toothed cat fossils, are in which city?
questions.fact: The saber-toothed cat Smilodon has been California's official state fossil since 1973.
questions.src: capitolmuseum.ca.gov state-symbols fossil-saber-toothed-cat (AB 940, 1973; Rancho La Brea tar pits, Los Angeles)

questions.q: Pterosaurs, the flying reptiles of the dinosaur age, had wings made of what?
questions.fact: Pterosaurs weren't dinosaurs, but close reptile cousins and the first animals with backbones to fly.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pterosaur (membrane on extremely long fourth finger; earliest vertebrates known to have evolved powered flight); britannica.com/animal/pterosaur (not dinosaurs)

questions.q: The sail-backed Dimetrodon is often mistaken for a dinosaur. It was actually closer kin to what?
questions.fact: It died out some 40 million years before the first dinosaurs appeared.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimetrodon (synapsid, more closely related to mammals than to dinosaurs; 294-271 Ma; extinct some 40 million years before dinosaurs appeared)
